newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Calls active in Commercial Union.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Calls active in Commercial Union.

text.p: Renewed speculation of consolidation in the insurance industry prompted a flurry of activity in options on Commercial Union in an otherwise listless derivatives market, dealers said.
They noted out-of-the-money call buying, which forced the shares up 36-1/2p to 692-1/2p by 1537 GMT.
"There's still talk of takeovers in the sector. It seems like rubbish to me, but people are buying calls just in case," said one.
More than 800 of the 900 Commercial Union options that traded were in out-of-the-money calls.
Most of the volume was in the January 700 calls, where more than 400 lots changed hands.
Dealers also noted a buyer of some 2,000 December 390 calls on Lloyds tsb. Shares in Lloyds were up 2p to 402-1/2p.
Trading in FTSE 100 index options was light and implied volatility crept higher as dealers waited for the Chancellor to deliver the budget.
Dealers said they expect index volatility to ease tomorrow afternoon. The FTSE 100 was up 32.8 points at 4,087.4.
